vibe.rationale: Vibe 5 — third consecutive session hold at this level (June 22 evening, June 23 morning, June 23 evening). The Vibe 5 designation reflects a Hormuz arc that is making measurable progress toward normalization while being offset by new structural negatives on domestic and long-range environmental axes. Positive movement 1 (Lebanon ceasefire hour 24): The ceasefire has survived its first full day nominally intact — no declared failure by either principal, no formal void announcement — placing it at approximately the critical midpoint of the 48-hour stability threshold. At hour ~24, the ceasefire is showing fragile-but-durable characteristics: both sides continue low-level tactical operations (Israel striking Lebanese infrastructure it characterizes as operational necessity; Hezbollah anti-tank responses) without either triggering a formal ceasefire-void declaration. This is the expected fragile-but-intact holding pattern. If it survives through June 24 evening (hour 48), Iran's stated procedural rationale for the re-closure claim dissolves and the Switzerland formal Round 1 scheduling becomes politically feasible. Positive movement 2 (Witkoff/Araghchi Swiss talks confirmed): The 60-day compliance window's most dangerous early-session risk — full diplomatic dark — has been avoided. Working-level technical contact at the Witkoff/Araghchi tier is confirmed, per CBS and JPost/Bloomberg reporting. This does not move the Lloyd's normalization gate, but it preserves the normalization pathway's institutional plumbing. Positive movement 3 (heat advisory expiring, weather relief T-1): The acute PNW fire-weather emergency is measurably resolving — the heat advisory ends tonight, the Gulf of Alaska low-pressure system arrives tomorrow, showers begin Thursday night. The Kartar Fire's acutest atmospheric risk window is closing naturally rather than through fire suppression achievement alone. WTI $74-76 range is directionally positive (modest decline from Monday's uncertainty premium open). New structural negative 1 (SCOTUS VRA ruling): Louisiana v. Callais 6-3 represents the most significant federal voting rights regression since Shelby County v. Holder (2013) — substantially raising the Section 2 evidentiary bar and immediately deploying the ruling to apply Alabama's discriminatory map in the 2026 election cycle. Combined with still-outstanding rulings on birthright citizenship (14th Amendment) and mail ballot counting (direct November 2026 midterm implications), the domestic legal axis has added material new uncertainty to the brief's risk landscape. New structural negative 2 (Super El Niño warning): The KLCC June 22 reporting on a forming Super El Niño introduces a 2026-2027 critically dry PNW winter as a structural threat that compounds the existing four-drought-year cycle, record-low snowpack, and 2026 fire season in a forward risk frame that is categorically worse than any individual current emergency. New structural negative 3 (Amazon WA 2,198 WARN layoffs): The confirmed Washington State WARN filing for 2,198 Amazon corporate positions (April 28-June; ~one-third software engineers) adds concrete regional economic displacement to the abstract $200B capex-vs-headcount paradox — the PNW tech employment base is contracting in headcount even as capital investment accelerates into AI infrastructure. Upgrade to Vibe 6 requires: Lebanon ceasefire holds clean 48 hours (through ~June 24 evening); Witkoff/Araghchi contact produces formal Round 1 scheduling announcement or Swiss joint statement with Iran; Iran formally retracts or conditionally suspends the Hormuz re-closure declaration; WTI breaks and holds below $74 (deal-day low). Drop to Vibe 4 requires: Lebanon ceasefire formal collapse with Iran reinstating physical Hormuz enforcement posture; Kartar Fire rapid acreage escalation (above 20,000 acres with structure threats) under Red Flag conditions; SCOTUS birthright citizenship ruling eliminates 14th Amendment birthright guarantee; Reconciliation 2.0 full HFC revolt preventing Rules Committee action within the T-7 window.

items.summary: The June 23 evening Hormuz picture represents the most positive operational position of the post-MOU contested compliance period, while stopping short of the upgrade thresholds established in the morning brief. The Lebanon ceasefire has survived to approximately hour 24 of the 48-hour stability threshold without either principal party declaring the ceasefire void. Low-level violations by both Israel and Hezbollah continue — Israeli strikes on Lebanese infrastructure characterized by Israel as operational necessity; Hezbollah anti-tank targeting of Israeli armor in response — but neither the Israeli government nor Hezbollah's political-military command has issued a formal ceasefire-void declaration. This is the fragile-but-nominally-intact holding pattern that, if sustained through approximately June 24 evening (hour 48), dissolves Iran's stated procedural rationale for the Hormuz re-closure claim. At hour ~24, the ceasefire is at the critical midpoint. The operative positive development of the June 23 session is the confirmed Witkoff/Araghchi Switzerland technical contact. CBS News confirmed that US and Iranian negotiators met in Switzerland. The Jerusalem Post (citing Bloomberg) reported both US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had traveled to Switzerland for working-level nuclear technical talks. President Trump simultaneously issued public maximalist pressure — stating publicly he would 'hit Iran very hard again' over continued Hezbollah activity in Lebanon — a classic dual-track pressure posture (technical engagement at the diplomatic level, maximalist threat in public) that has characterized the entire negotiation arc. The key analytical distinction: this is confirmed working-level technical contact at the Witkoff/Araghchi tier, NOT the formal Vance-level Round 1 framework session that was canceled June 22. Iran has not lifted its stated condition for formal talks (Lebanon war halt); the proceeding of working-level contact without that condition being formally satisfied suggests Iran is engaging technically while maintaining the legal-political re-closure claim as leverage. The 60-day nuclear compliance window (Day 4) has not gone diplomatically dark — a meaningful positive over the full-dark scenario that the June 22 evening brief's 'CANCELED' framing suggested. Iran's formal Hormuz re-closure declaration has not been retracted as of this session. The contested compliance status remains operative. Lloyd's war-risk normalization cannot be announced while Iran and CENTCOM maintain contradictory Strait-status positions. The Lloyd's normalization pathway — Lebanon ceasefire 48h clean → Iran re-closure retracted → Switzerland formal Round 1 rescheduled → Lloyd's normalization — is at Step 1, hour 24. WTI is trading in the $74-76 range, a modest decline from Monday's $76.46 uncertainty-premium open. This is directionally consistent with ceasefire stability credit being priced in; the $74 deal-day low remains the operative normalization confidence floor — if WTI breaks below $74 and holds, it would signal market confidence in the normalization trajectory. PGSA transit fees continue waived during the 60-day window with registration mandatory; CENTCOM transit count continues operative through Day 4 with no confirmed physical interdiction. The 118-tanker stuck backlog and Kpler's 40-transit/day forward projection remain forward projections awaiting Lloyd's normalization actualization.

items.summary: Four secondary geopolitical threads on June 23 evening. First: Colombia's presidential escrutinio advances through its second day with no certification announcement. The preconteo result — de la Espriella 49.65% vs. Cepeda 48.70% — stands as the working count with approximately 99.9% of mesas tallied. Iván Cepeda's 'no binding value' contest position remains operative through the judicial review phase. No evidence of certification reversal or counting irregularity sufficient to overturn the 0.95-point lead has emerged. A certified de la Espriella result would represent Trump's second consecutive post-deal Latin America alignment outcome alongside the expected Peru Fujimori certification. Escrutinio timelines in Colombian election law typically resolve within days to two weeks of the runoff date (June 21). Second: Ukraine-Russia peace talks are formally deadlocked entering the June 23 evening cycle. Russia rejected European conditions for dialogue on June 11 — characterizing EU/Ukraine joint negotiating positions as 'completely unacceptable.' Zelenskyy's June 4 open letter proposing an immediate frontline ceasefire and 'all-for-all' prisoner exchange has received no formal response from Moscow. The US-brokered three-day Victory Day ceasefire (May 8-9) expired without follow-through; Geneva-format talks have produced no substantive breakthrough. The frontline combat continues as a grinding attritional engagement. No formal multilateral session is scheduled. The Ukraine-Russia arc is the briefing series' longest-running secondary geopolitical thread without a resolution pathway within the current session horizon. Third: Peru ONPE advances to Day 17 of uncertified results — Sanchez 50.10% vs. Fujimori 49.90%; full official count expected early July. Fourth: New York and Maryland are holding congressional and gubernatorial primaries today (June 23). In New York, Governor Kathy Hochul faces re-election on the Democratic side; Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman is the Trump-endorsed Republican candidate. Contested congressional primaries in NY-3, NY-4, NY-12, NY-17, and NY-19 are active — these are House balance districts with direct implications for the November 2026 majority calculus. Maryland is holding comparable down-ballot contests. Results were arriving but not fully tabulated as of brief time.

items.summary: The June 23 evening economic and energy picture reflects partial positive movement directionally consistent with Lebanon ceasefire stability reducing the Hormuz uncertainty premium, while remaining inside the contested compliance range that prevents Lloyd's normalization and confirmed pump relief. WTI is trading in approximately the $74-76 range on Tuesday evening — a modest decline from Monday's $76.46 uncertainty-premium open — consistent with partial ceasefire stability credit being priced in. Movement toward $74 (the June 19 MOU deal-day low establishing the normalization confidence floor) is directionally positive. If WTI breaks below $74 and sustains, it would constitute the market confidence signal that the June 21 brief identified as the commercial gateway indicator. However, $74 has not been breached on a sustained basis as of this session; Lloyd's war-risk rate normalization remains blocked by the operative Iran re-closure declaration. Iran's formal contested compliance claim prevents any insurance normalization announcement regardless of WTI direction. The pump relief timeline — Oregon ~$5.35, national ~$4.56 gasoline — requires Lloyd's normalization as the upstream gate before refinery-to-pump transport lag delivers retail price relief. That timeline, projected at mid-to-late July contingent on a June normalization announcement, is sliding toward late July as a contested compliance hold. On the macro framework: the June 17 FOMC decision under incoming Chair Kevin Warsh held the federal funds rate at 3.50-3.75% for a fourth consecutive meeting, but the dot plot's hawkish revision (9 of 19 officials seeing at least one hike this year; median year-end fed funds 3.8%) remains the dominant driver for equity markets over the Hormuz narrative. The Fed revised its 2026 PCE inflation forecast sharply upward to 3.6% (from 2.7% in March) and trimmed GDP growth to 2.2% — citing supply shocks including Middle East energy disruptions as contributing factors. The FEC (Foreign Entity of Concern) regulatory framework — barring entities tied to China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran from US clean energy tax credits — is generating compounding supply chain shocks in solar panels, EV batteries, and critical minerals, as US manufacturers scramble to requalify suppliers and absorb cost increases. These FEC tariff shocks are feeding the energy-adjacent CPI components that Warsh cited repeatedly in his June 17 press conference and are structurally resistant to the Hormuz disinflation impulse: even with Hormuz normalization, FEC-driven materials cost inflation would persist. The broader inflationary picture (May CPI headline 4.2% YoY, core 2.9% YoY) and Q1 GDP revised to 1.6% annualized constitute the macroeconomic backdrop against which the Warsh SEP hawkishness is set.

Reconciliation 2.0 was not on the agenda. The Freedom Caucus 'major changes' demand to the Senate version remains unresolved through Tuesday evening. The July 4 abortion-provider-funding lapse — the most powerful available base-politics forcing function — has not been deployed as the primary whip argument entering the final critical week. The narrowing window (T-7 to Rules Committee action by June 30) with the forcing function still unactivated is the Reconciliation 2.0 arc's most acute risk indicator. The 30-day AI pathway explanation deadline falls approximately July 18 (T-25 days); the 60-day justify/reform deadline falls approximately August 17. The 2,198 positions (April 28-June 2026; approximately one-third software engineers) are part of more than 30,000 corporate positions Amazon has eliminated since October 2025 — while simultaneously committing $200 billion in 2026 capital expenditure, predominantly on AI data center infrastructure. The structural divergence — capital accelerating into AI infrastructure while headcount contracts — is the dominant Seattle-region labor market dynamic. Microsoft's comparable posture (FY2026 H1 capex $72.4 billion, primarily data centers) reinforces the regional pattern. Fourth: Secure America Act (DHS $70 billion) advances to Law Day 10 — ICE/CBP deployment infrastructure operationalizing.

items.summary: The June 23 evening infrastructure picture represents the transition point between the heat-advisory acute risk period and the weather relief window. The NWS Heat Advisory for Western Washington expires at 11:00 PM tonight — this is the final hour. Red Flag Warnings remain in effect across eastern Washington through tonight, with westerly Cascade gap winds continuing. The Kartar Fire near Omak (Okanogan County) has passed through the session's primary acute risk window: the daytime hours of June 23 (approximately 10am-7pm Pacific) under Red Flag Warning Day 2 constituted the highest-consequence fire-behavior test of the week. As of brief time, the evening ICS-209 incident report with updated acreage and containment data from the afternoon suppression cycle has not yet been released. The last confirmed data — approximately 11,700 acres and 15% containment from the June 21 incident report — should be updated in the evening ICS-209 cycle. The 283 personnel assigned to the Kartar Fire have been working containment lines along Kartar Road and the northern perimeter using backburn operations; the afternoon heating test's outcome will be reflected in the evening report. Level 3 evacuations remain in effect for Kartar Valley, Kartar Valley Road, Columbia River Road near Omak Lake, and the south end of Omak Lake Road. The six-fire concurrent situation in Washington State: Tule Road Fire (24,090 acres, 95% contained) is approaching resolution; Juniper Dunes (90% contained) near resolution; Upriver Fire (75% contained) in mop-up under local agency control since June 22. Oregon's wildfire emergency (Executive Order 26-10, signed June 15) remains active with 414 fires and 8,000+ acres burned YTD — Oregon's concurrent fire load is tracking alongside Washington's elevated season. NIFC National Preparedness Level 3 (raised June 18) is Day 5 as of this session. The dominant positive signal for the infrastructure domain is weather relief at T-1 day: the Gulf of Alaska low-pressure system is projected to arrive Wednesday June 24, with cooler temperatures and strengthening onshore flow, and showers beginning Thursday night June 25 through the weekend. If the forecast holds, the acute fire-weather window ends after tonight — one more day of Red Flag conditions before natural relief. East Cascades fire onset (June 29-July 1) is T-6 days; the Kartar Fire is already inside the onset region. BPA grid remained stable through Day 2 of the heat advisory; no forced outages reported in the June 23 cycle.

items.summary: Secondary infrastructure threads on June 23 evening. First: FERC's June 18 emergency orders for AI data center grid interconnection advance to Day 5 of the 30/60-day show cause timeline. The FERC emergency action — reducing grid interconnection timelines for AI data centers from multi-year processes to approximately 90 days — was issued in response to a NERC Level 3 alert triggered by abrupt data center demand shifts in Virginia and Texas. US data centers currently account for approximately 5% of national electricity demand, with projections to reach 15% by 2035; Virginia's data center concentration already accounts for 25% of the state's total demand. The show cause orders targeting the largest interconnection queue entries require AI infrastructure pathway explanations by approximately July 18 (T-25 days) and full justification or reform commitments by approximately August 17 (T-55 days). These orders are structurally separate from but related to the broader grid interconnection backlog — gigawatts of ready-to-build generation projects waiting years for interconnection studies, with transmission lines requiring a decade or more of permitting and construction. The PJM 13-state grid operator serving the mid-Atlantic and Midwest is facing structural questions about its capacity to absorb projected AI data center load growth. Second: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory is approximately T-5 days from end-of-June removal (~June 28). This coastal atmospheric anchor — providing real-time meteorological data for Pacific Northwest fire-weather modeling — is entering its final operational days. The monitoring gap opening ~June 28 coincides with the east Cascades T-6 fire onset window, the Kartar Fire's active suppression phase, and the pre-July 4 holiday congestion. Third: Longview CSB advances to Day 29. The final night of the heat advisory reopens the elevated structural monitoring flag for the 90,000-gallon hazardous material storage facility; the acute vapor pressure risk window from the June 14-16 event remains formally closed. Fourth: Upriver Fire mop-up advances to Day 2 under full local agency control. The heat advisory's final night is the last major atmospheric test for the Upriver perimeter before natural weather relief arrives.

items.headline: SCOTUS 6-3 — Louisiana v. Callais: VRA Section 2 Bar Substantially Raised; Alabama Discriminatory Map Immediately Applied; Senate Legislative Response Initiated; Birthright Citizenship And Mail Ballot Rulings OUTSTANDING (Days To Term End)
items.summary: The June 23 session's most consequential domestic development is the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, which substantially raised the evidentiary bar for proving Section 2 Voting Rights Act violations — making it significantly more difficult for communities of color to challenge racially discriminatory congressional maps. The ruling's operative legal change is the elevation of the Section 2 discriminatory-purpose or discriminatory-effects standard, requiring plaintiffs to meet a higher burden of proof than the framework that had governed VRA Section 2 litigation since Thornburg v. Gingles (1986). The immediate practical consequence was equally significant: the Court issued an unsigned order allowing Alabama to use a congressional map that a lower federal court had already found to be racially discriminatory in the 2026 elections — deploying the new Louisiana v. Callais standard to override a sitting lower-court injunction. Civil rights organizations, including Common Cause, characterized the ruling as an effective gutting of the VRA's remaining enforcement machinery. The ruling follows Shelby County v. Holder (2013) as the most significant VRA regression in the statute's 60-year history. The Senate legislative response has been initiated — Senate Democrats, including Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, are exploring pathways to a new Voting Rights Act to restore Section 2's pre-Callais enforcement posture. The legislative prospects in the current Congress depend on the Senate filibuster calculation and whether any Republican senators break on procedural grounds; as of this session, prospects are uncertain. The Louisiana v. Callais ruling carries direct November 2026 midterm implications: districts in Alabama, Louisiana, and potentially Texas, North Carolina, and Georgia that are subject to pending Section 2 litigation could see the existing legal challenges dismissed or weakened under the new evidentiary standard, altering the competitive landscape in multiple House seats currently classified as contested. Two additional high-stakes SCOTUS rulings remain outstanding with the Court's term ending imminently: Trump v. United States (birthright citizenship — testing the administration's attempt to end birthright citizenship; direct 14th Amendment implications) and Watson v. Republican National Committee (mail ballot counting — whether states can continue counting mail ballots postmarked by Election Day; direct November 2026 midterm operational implications). Both rulings are expected within days. Combined with Louisiana v. Callais, these three decisions constitute the most concentrated domestic legal risk event of the session.

items.summary: The June 23 evening marks the Pacific Northwest's transition out of the acute heat and fire-weather emergency period into the pre-relief window. The NWS Heat Advisory for Western Washington expires at 11:00 PM tonight — the final hours of a two-day event. Red Flag Warnings remain in effect across eastern Washington through tonight's advisory expiration. The Kartar Fire (Okanogan County, near Omak) has passed through today's primary acute risk window — the daytime solar heating cycle under Red Flag Warning Day 2 — and is now in the evening reporting gap before the ICS-209 incident report cycle provides updated acreage and containment data. The last confirmed data (approximately 11,700 acres, 15% containment from June 21) will be updated in tonight's reporting. Level 3 evacuations remain in effect for the Kartar Valley corridor. Weather relief is T-1 day — the Gulf of Alaska low-pressure system arrives Wednesday, with Thursday night showers the operative fire-weather relief mechanism. The acute fire-weather window compresses after tonight to one remaining day (tomorrow) before natural conditions shift. Oregon is carrying a concurrent wildfire burden under Governor Kotek's Executive Order 26-10 (June 15, Day 8): 414 fires and 8,000+ acres burned YTD as of mid-June. NIFC National Preparedness Level 3 (Day 5) covers both states. The east Cascades fire onset window (June 29-July 1, T-6 days) is the next major PNW structural fire-risk event; Kartar Fire is already inside that regional envelope. BPA's grid maintained stability through Day 2 of the heat advisory without forced outages — the drought-year-4 hydropower constraint has not triggered a reliability event through the peak demand period. Portland recorded approximately 95-100°F on June 23; Seattle approximately 90°F — consistent with the advisory forecast and approaching (but not definitively breaking) historic daily records.

items.summary: Secondary PNW environmental and local threads on June 23 evening. First and most structurally significant: The Super El Niño warning reported by KLCC/Oregon Public Broadcasting on June 22 introduces a critically dry 2026-2027 Pacific Northwest winter as an emerging structural threat. A Super El Niño pattern — characterized by sea surface temperature anomalies in the central-eastern tropical Pacific exceeding +2.0°C sustained across multiple months — would bring a warm, dry Pacific Northwest winter with dramatically reduced snowpack accumulation. For a region in its fourth consecutive drought year with 50% of normal statewide snowpack already entering the 2026 fire season, a Super El Niño winter would generate a fifth-year drought cycle with 2027 fire season conditions potentially exceeding 2026's early-season outbreak. El Niño base probability stands at 61%; super El Niño at approximately 25% (1-in-4). This long-range signal does not change the immediate Kartar Fire or heat advisory calculus, but it is categorically the most consequential environmental development of the brief cycle for PNW resilience planning horizons. Second: Washington drought emergency Day 19 (fourth consecutive year; 50% statewide snowpack; 12 emergency counties). Oregon drought at 83% of state affected. The Thursday weather relief (showers beginning Thursday night) will provide minimal structural drought value — fine fuel moisture benefit but no meaningful aquifer recharge. Third: Amazon's Washington State WARN filing (2,198 positions, April 28-June) represents the most direct recent data point on the PNW tech-labor market contraction. Combined with Microsoft's data-center-focused capital deployment ($72.4B H1 FY2026 capex) and Amazon's own $200B 2026 capex commitment, the regional pattern is a structural bifurcation: AI-era capital investment accelerating while white-collar employment contracts. University of Washington is accelerating AI curriculum in response. Fourth: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory at T-5 days from end-of-June removal (~June 28). The atmospheric monitoring gap opens precisely during the Kartar Fire's active suppression phase and the east Cascades T-6 onset window. Fifth: Southern Resident Orca L-pod calf is expected to be entering its third week of confirmed survival as of this session — continued positive signal for the critically endangered Southern Resident population. NOAA Pacific gray whale coastal washup pace continues above annual average (Oregon 21 YTD, Washington 17 YTD). Sixth: The Embassy Suites Pioneer Square labor dispute (UNITE HERE Local 8) enters its final night under heat advisory conditions — heat-adjacent labor safety considerations remain in force through tonight's 11pm expiration. Seventh: Echinococcus multilocularis peri-urban spread surveillance in Washington State coyote populations continues active.

analyst_summary: June 23, 2026 evening holds at Vibe 5 — the third consecutive session at this level, spanning June 22 evening through June 23 morning and evening. The session's central analytical tension is between measurable positive movement on the Hormuz normalization arc and two new structural negatives on previously quieter axes: the SCOTUS Louisiana v. Callais 6-3 VRA ruling, and the emerging Super El Niño warning for 2026-2027. On Hormuz: the Lebanon ceasefire has survived to approximately hour 24 of the 48-hour stability threshold without declared failure. Witkoff and Araghchi have conducted confirmed working-level nuclear technical talks in Switzerland — CBS reported negotiators met; the 60-day window has not gone diplomatically dark. WTI has moved modestly toward the $74 normalization confidence floor. These developments are directionally correct and each necessary for the normalization pathway, but none is individually sufficient: Iran's re-closure declaration remains operative, Lloyd's normalization is blocked, and the formal Round 1 framework session has no rescheduled date. The 48-hour ceasefire test clears through tomorrow evening; if it holds, the operative upgrade logic engages. On the new structural negatives: Louisiana v. Callais is the most significant federal voting rights regression since Shelby County v. Holder (2013), deploying a substantially higher Section 2 evidentiary standard immediately to Alabama's discriminatory map and altering the competitive landscape for multiple House districts under pending VRA challenge. Combined with still-outstanding rulings on birthright citizenship and mail ballot counting — both with direct November 2026 midterm implications — the domestic legal axis is at peak uncertainty concentration for the term. The Super El Niño warning places a critically dry PNW winter on the 2026-2027 structural horizon: compounding four consecutive drought years and record-low snowpack in a forward risk frame that exceeds any current-season emergency management posture. On the PNW fire front: the heat advisory is expiring tonight, weather relief arrives tomorrow, and the Kartar Fire's daytime spread test outcome is pending in the evening ICS-209 cycle. The acute fire-weather window closes to one remaining day before natural relief. Three primary watchitems for June 24: first, Lebanon ceasefire 48-hour threshold — the operative upgrade condition approaches June 24 evening; clean clearance dissolves Iran's re-closure rationale and opens the Switzerland formal Round 1 rescheduling pathway; second, Kartar Fire evening ICS-209 update — the post-daytime spread test acreage and containment will confirm whether the 283-person suppression team held the 15%-containment perimeter through the Red Flag Day 2 window; third, SCOTUS remaining rulings — birthright citizenship and mail ballot decisions are expected within days of June 23, with the full domestic legal risk event concentrated in the final days of the term.
